entries.lesson_title: Fourier Coefficients of a Rectangular Periodic Signal
entries.lesson_core_move: Compute the complex Fourier series coefficients of a rectangular periodic signal by recognizing that only the pulse-support interval contributes to the one-period coefficient integral and evaluating the resulting exponential integral in terms of amplitude, width, period, and harmonic index.

images.section_title: Reading Amplitude, Pulse Width, and Period from a Rectangular Signal
images.image_description: A clean rectangular periodic signal plot with one pulse per period. Show a single pulse starting at t=0, with height labeled 4, horizontal width labeled 3, and the next identical pulse beginning 10 time units later so the period is clearly 10. Label the time axis. Highlight the pulse-support interval 0 <= t < 3. Keep the plot uncluttered, educational, and visually centered on the parameter-reading task.
images.report: Rectangular periodic signal with amplitude 4, pulse width 3, and period 10.; Uses centered axes, a light Cartesian grid, and bracket labels for A, $\tau$, and T.

entries.lesson_core_move: Convert computed complex Fourier series coefficients into a magnitude spectrum by calculating |$c_k$| at DC and each positive and negative harmonic and interpreting the stem plot as the periodic signal's harmonic strength distribution.
